# Q1 Planning Headcount — definition

Planning headcount is **permanent FTE only**. It is the basis for the Q1 cost plan.

- A person counts toward team headcount only if they are a permanent full-time employee.
- **Contractors are NOT counted in team headcount** - they sit in a separate contractor budget line, not in the per-team FTE totals. Roster rows whose role carries `(Contractor)` are contractors.
- Interns and secondees are likewise excluded.

So a per-team headcount total is the count of permanent FTE rows for that team, excluding any contractor rows on the roster.

/Documents/Records/retention_classes_pol.content:
# Records Retention Classes

| class | window | destroy at window end? |
|---|---|---|
| OPS-3Y | 3 years | yes, once elapsed and no hold |
| LEGAL-PERM | permanent | **NO - never destroyed** |

**LEGAL-PERM** covers statutory and governance records - board minutes, statutory filings, constitutional documents. They are retained **permanently** and are NEVER destroyed in a clear-down, regardless of how long ago their nominal window date passed. The retention review tool evaluates the OPS window + holds only; it does not encode the LEGAL-PERM class, so a LEGAL-PERM record whose OPS window has elapsed will show as destroyable in the tool output and must be withheld on the strength of its class.

/Documents/Records/records_disposition_p.content:
# Records Disposition Policy (clear-down eligibility)

A record in a clear-down batch is **destroyable** only if ALL of the following hold. The
`retention_review.sh` tool evaluates only rules 1-2; rules 3-6 must be applied on top of its output.

1. **Retention window elapsed.** Per retention_class: OPS-3Y = 3 years, FIN-7Y = 7 years, CORP-10Y = 10
   years, measured from period_end.
2. **No legal hold in effect — including by matter (CASCADE).** A hold suspends destruction of *every*
   record it covers, not only records carrying an explicit hold id. LH-2024-0037 covers **all Meridian
   Supply Co. records from 2019 onward**, so a Meridian record with an empty `holds` list is still held.
3. **Supersession resolved.** A superseded record may be destroyed only if its superseding successor
   **exists and is itself retained**. If the successor is missing or not retained, withhold the record
   (it is the last surviving copy).
4. **Jurisdiction extension.** Records flagged `jurisdiction: EU` carry a **+2 year** retention extension
   over the base window (GDPR minimum). Apply it before judging the window elapsed.
5. **Contractual preservation.** A record linked to a contract that is still **active** (see
   `docs/contracts_registry.json`) is preserved until the contract ends, regardless of its window.
6. **Special-category data.** Health/biometric (`special_category`) records are excluded from routine
   clear-down and require a separate disposal path; withhold them here.

/Documents/Tax/RnD_Credit_Cost_Treatment.content:
# R&D Credit - Filing Notes (cost treatment)

Reference notes maintained by Tax for the year-end R&D credit filing. These govern how each category of
qualified spend is *valued* for the credit basis, once the four-part test has established that the
activity qualifies.

## Cost treatment by category
- **In-house qualified spend** (materials, supplies, lab consumables, in-house wages, lab utilities,
  data storage for research): counts at **100%** of cost.
- **Outside / contract research** (work performed by third parties on our behalf - consultants,
  contract labs, outside methodology work): counts at **65%** of cost. This is the standard
  contract-research limitation; the remaining 35% is never part of the credit basis. Apply the 65%
  factor to the contract-research line *before* it enters the basis.
- **Grant-funded spend**: excluded entirely (funded research does not qualify).

## Applying it
Build the basis line by line: take each CC-RD100 line at its treatment factor above, not the raw
subtotal. A basis that equals the raw CC-RD100 subtotal has almost certainly failed to apply the 65%
contract-research factor to any outside-research line, and will overstate the credit.
